h2: Plumber & Pool Service in Nusa Dua – Villa Care You Can Trust
intro: Looking for a reliable plumber and pool service in Nusa Dua? Bali Fix handles everything from dripping taps to cloudy overflow pools across Tanjung Benoa, Bualu, Sawangan, Kampial and Peminge. Send photos on WhatsApp and we'll scope out the job before any work begins.

sections.h3: Salt Air, Hard Water – What Wears Down Fast Here
sections.text: The coastal breeze and Bukit water supply create a tough environment for plumbing and pool hardware. Fittings corrode faster than inland, limescale builds up inside heaters and pump seals, and overflow channels clog with mineral deposits. If your villa sits near Tanjung Benoa or Bualu, you'll notice this within a few months without regular attention. Bali Fix inspects these vulnerable points during every visit so small issues don't become expensive repairs.

sections.h3: What Villa Owners in Nusa Dua Message Us About Most
sections.text: Large resort-style pools with overflows, waterfalls and spa jets demand constant chemical balancing and equipment checks. In gated estates like Sawangan and Kampial, the most common calls involve blocked drains after heavy rain, leaking water heaters, and septic tank backups. Bathroom fixtures in spacious villas also fail more often because of the hard water. Whether it's a single dripping tap or a full pool renovation, WhatsApp us photos and we'll scope out the job.

sections.h3: Plumber & Pool Service Across Every Nusa Dua Neighbourhood
sections.text: Bali Fix covers all of Nusa Dua: Tanjung Benoa, Bualu, Sawangan, Kampial and Peminge. Many complexes here operate under strict access rules – gate codes, security check-ins, and limited working hours for outside contractors. Scheduling work in advance means we arrive with the right parts and respect the estate's timeline. For villa managers juggling multiple properties, bundling visits saves time and keeps every unit guest-ready.

sections.h3: Dry Season vs Wet Season – Pool & Plumbing Tips
sections.text: During the dry months (April–October), evaporation accelerates and pool chemistry shifts quickly – top up levels and test pH at least twice a week. In the wet season, expect more blocked drains, pump overloads from debris, and septic issues after prolonged rain. A quick pre-season check of filters, overflow channels and heater elements catches problems before they strand you mid-stay. Message us on WhatsApp whenever something looks off; early fixes are always simpler.
